title: Showcase Wall vs Peer Recognition Activity
panelPrompt: Click a format to see which recognition goal it fits.

image.style: flat vector comparison poster, warm friendly icons, muted textbook palette
image.overall: A two-column comparison poster about two ways of recognising student work. Each column is a tall rounded panel with a coloured header bar carrying its printed title, and a clean flat illustration below. The two printed headers, and the ONLY text in the image, are: "Student Showcase Wall" (left) and "Peer Recognition Activity" (right).
image.layoutNotes: Divide the content area into 2 equal-width vertical columns with a clear gutter of background between each pair. Every column must have the SAME width, top edge, and bottom edge so the overlay's hover zones line up exactly. Each column has its printed header in bold dark text at the very top, on a tinted header bar in that column's accent colour, with simple flat icons below. No other text anywhere. Leave at least 4% margin at the left and right edges and 8% at top and bottom. With only two columns each panel is wide, so draw one larger scene per column rather than a cluster of small icons.

zones.label: Student Showcase Wall
zones.summary: A standing display of finished work.
facts: Bulletin board, photo album, or webpage
Visible to parents and visitors, not just club members
Gives a student's work a life beyond the session it was built in
Pairs each project with the student's name and a one-sentence description

draw.position: The left column, roughly 4% to 47% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted blue. Below it: a cork bulletin board on a wall with six pinned cards showing small abstract project thumbnails and blank caption bars beneath each (no readable words), with two adult visitor silhouettes looking at it from one side.

zones.label: Peer Recognition Activity
facts: A shout-out circle or kudos card at the end of a session
Recognition comes from peers, not a mentor
Happens frequently, in minutes rather than as a standing display
Lands differently because it comes from someone facing the same challenges
Costs almost nothing to run every week

draw.position: The right column, roughly 53% to 96% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted green. Below it: five student figures seated in a circle facing inward, with small speech bubbles and a couple of small hand-passed cards between them, and a small clock icon showing a short duration.

quiz.question: Which format is visible to parents and visitors?
Which format happens every session in a few minutes?
